summary: Yang–Zhao prove a cohomological Milnor formula and a fibration formula for relative cohomological characteristic classes, and deduce Saito's conjecture that the cohomological characteristic class equals the cycle class of the characteristic class for smooth quasi-projective schemes over a perfect field (Theorem 6.13), with the curve case first (Corollary 6.6). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item (Saito's conjecture added as a statement), every missing item is routed exactly once, and nine findings are recorded against arXiv v4. The proof errors E6 and E8 are repaired; none affects a stated result. Not formalised.

conventions: Base convention B: S Noetherian, all displayed S-schemes separated of finite type; Λ a commutative Noetherian ring killed by an integer invertible on S. All tensor, Hom and six-operation notation is derived. Dctf means bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes; no unconditional perfectness over a group ring is inferred.
Diagram convention D: Z --τ--> X --f--> Y --g--> S, τ closed, h=g f, U=X\Z. δ:Y→Y×S Y, i:X×Y X→X×S X, δ1:X→X×Y X, δ0=iδ1.

C1: K_Y/S=g!Λ is locally constant and its canonical evaluation K_Y/S⊗δ!Λ→Λ is an isomorphism. C2: H^0(Z,K_Z/Y)=H^1(Z,K_Z/Y)=0. C3: F∈Dctf(X,Λ), h is F-ULA and f|U is F|U-ULA. Smooth g implies C1, not C2.

Application convention A: k perfect of characteristic p>0, Λ finite local with residue characteristic ℓ≠p. Integers in local cohomological identities mean their image in Λ. dim and Swan for complexes are alternating invariants after derived residue-field reduction, not sums of nonnegative Betti numbers.

An item’s hypotheses and explicitly referenced conventions form part of its statement. Proposed tests are specification tests, not executed Lean proofs. ExternalInputs/gaps are unresolved proof leaves, not theorem assumptions silently declaring a result built.

All locators without a named external source use arXiv2209.11086v4. PFF numbering is explicitly marked. General-base results are not claimed covered by EDC’s field-only coefficient/constructibility conventions.

Coefficient extension Λ→B (Q01–Q10) and geometric field extension k→k' (M14) are separate: the former needs faithful finite freeness, without invertible degree; the latter argument cancels its degree in Λ-cohomology and retains the prime-to-ℓ hypothesis.

items.statement: For diagram(2.3.1), H on Y,G on T, pullback of c_{δ,f,H,G} by h agrees with c_{δ,fg,g*H,G} followed by exceptional base change.

items.name: Direct-image compatibility of c
items.statement: For diagram(2.3.1), F on Y',G on T, the square(2.3.4) commutes using ordinary base change and the natural tensor-to-pushforward map; use δ!G, not δ!Λ, throughout its left side. No properness is imposed just to construct this comparison.

items.name: Smooth transversality
items.statement: In T01, if δ is smooth of pure relative dimension d, c_{δ,f,F,G} is an isomorphism and agrees with i*F⊗i*f*G(d)[2d]→i!(F⊗f*G) from smooth purity.

items.name: ULA implies transversality
items.statement: In T01, if f is F-ULA then c_{δ,f,F,G} is an isomorphism for every G; reduce using smooth factorization and the localization triangle to strong local acyclicity.

items.name: Alteration-test converse to local acyclicity
items.statement: For f:Y→T finite type over a field, if every test T'→T proper generically finite with T' and W smooth over a finite extension and W→T' closed has the base-changed F-transversality of diagram(2.5.1), then f is F-locally acyclic. This is an unused converse, not a proof prerequisite for later items.

items.name: Diagonal evaluation and C1
items.statement: For separated finite-type g:Y→S under B, construct K_Y/S⊗δ!Λ→Λ by tensor-exchange and diagonal adjunction. C1 is local constancy of K_Y/S plus invertibility of this particular map; it holds for smooth g.

api.name: YangZhao25.T10.spec
api.statement: For separated finite-type g:Y→S under B, construct K_Y/S⊗δ!Λ→Λ by tensor-exchange and diagonal adjunction. C1 is local constancy of K_Y/S plus invertibility of this particular map; it holds for smooth g.

api.name: YangZhao25.T10.characterisation
api.statement: Expose the diagonal evaluation map whose invertibility is part of C1.

api.name: YangZhao25.T10.compatibility
api.statement: For g smooth of dimension r compare its factors with Λ(r)[2r] and Λ(-r)[-2r].

tests.name: YangZhao25.T10.test1
tests.statement: For g=id the evaluation is Λ⊗Λ→Λ.

tests.name: YangZhao25.T10.test2
tests.statement: For Y=A1 over k, the twists/shifts cancel to Λ.

tests.name: YangZhao25.T10.test3

items.name: Dualizing transitivity under C1
items.statement: For X→Y→S under B and C1, f!Λ⊗f*K_Y/S→f!K_Y/S=K_X/S is an isomorphism.

items.name: Inverse diagonal twist
items.statement: Under T11's hypotheses, K_X/S⊗f*δ!Λ≃K_X/Y via c and diagonal evaluation.

items.name: ULA relative duality
items.statement: Under B, if G is Y-ULA then D_X/Y(G) is Y-ULA and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change in the stated finite-Tor coefficient setting.

items.name: External product preserves relative ULA
items.statement: For ULA objects over the two factors of a base product, their external derived tensor is ULA over the product; use the relative Künneth/local-acyclicity theorem, not just stalkwise tensor notation.

items.name: ULA diagonal tensor-dual comparison
items.statement: Under B,C1 and F,G∈Dctf(X/Y,Λ), F⊠Y D_X/Y(G)→i!(F⊠S D_X/S(G)) is an isomorphism, with its source identified by the inverse diagonal twist.

items.name: Regular-immersion fundamental-class extension
items.statement: Under B for regular η:P→Q of codimension c, construct Cl_η:Λ→η!Λ(c)[2c] and the self-intersection top Chern class. Do not assert Cl is an isomorphism for a singular ambient scheme without the source purity hypotheses.

api.statement: Under B for regular η:P→Q of codimension c, construct Cl_η:Λ→η!Λ(c)[2c] and the self-intersection top Chern class. Do not assert Cl is an isomorphism for a singular ambient scheme without the source purity hypotheses.

api.name: YangZhao25.T16.characterisation

api.name: YangZhao25.T16.compatibility
api.statement: Pullback to the regular immersion yields c_c of its normal bundle; composition and transverse base change are compatible.

items.name: Gysin map equals top-Chern action
items.statement: In the self-pullback square(2.9.1), δ regular of codimension r and Cl_δ invertible, the map on H0 induced by c_{δ,f,F} equals cup product with c_r(p*N_W/T^∨), where N is the conormal bundle. All twists and shifts use Cl_δ.

items.statement: In T01 with δ closed and j:T\W→T open, define δ^Δ(F)=i!(F⊗f*Rj*Λ). This explicit functorial model, not an arbitrary triangulated cone, is the defect of c_{δ,f,F,Λ}.

api.statement: In T01 with δ closed and j:T\W→T open, define δ^Δ(F)=i!(F⊗f*Rj*Λ). This explicit functorial model, not an arbitrary triangulated cone, is the defect of c_{δ,f,F,Λ}.

items.name: Characteristic class factors through K0
items.statement: Under B, C_X/S is additive on distinguished triangles of ULA objects, hence induces K0(X/S,Λ)→H0(X,K_X/S); a shift by one negates the class.

items.name: Locally free twist multiplies characteristic class
items.statement: Under B with X connected, F ULA/S and L locally constant finite free of constant rank r, C_X/S(F⊗L)=r C_X/S(F). The specialization C(L)=r C(Λ) requires Λ_X to be ULA/S. For general finite projective L use its trace-rank element, not an unspecified integer.

items.name: Unique extension across support vanishing
items.statement: Under B, if H0(Z,K_Z/S)=H1(Z,K_Z/S)=0 then restriction H0(X,K_X/S)→H0(U,K_U/S) is an isomorphism by the localization exact sequence.

items.name: Semipurity criterion for extension
items.statement: If X and S are smooth over a field, X→S has relative dimension r and codim_X Z>r, semipurity gives H0(Z,K_Z/S)=H1(Z,K_Z/S)=0.

items.name: Characteristic class with ULA only off Z
items.statement: Under B and C07’s two vanishings, for F∈Dctf(X,Λ) ULA/S on U, define C_X/S(F) as the unique extension of C_U/S(F|U). This class is not defined by choosing an arbitrary supported correction.

api.name: YangZhao25.C09.spec
api.statement: Under B and C07’s two vanishings, for F∈Dctf(X,Λ) ULA/S on U, define C_X/S(F) as the unique extension of C_U/S(F|U). This class is not defined by choosing an arbitrary supported correction.

api.name: YangZhao25.C09.characterisation
api.statement: Restriction to U is C_U/S(F|U) and uniquely characterizes the extension.

api.name: YangZhao25.C09.compatibility
api.statement: Enlarging the excluded support under the same two vanishings does not change the class.

tests.name: YangZhao25.C09.test2

tests.name: YangZhao25.C09.test3

items.name: Diagonal adjunction expression for characteristic class
items.statement: Under B and F ULA/S, C_X/S(F) is the adjoint of δ!Λ→RHom(pr2*F,pr1!F)→δ*K_X/S from identity and evaluation; it agrees with C04.

items.name: Arbitrary base change for relative characteristic classes
items.statement: For b:S'→S between Noetherian schemes and X'=X×S S', F ULA/S, the cohomology map induced by b_X*K_X/S→K_X'/S' sends C_X/S(F) to C_X'/S'(b_X*F).

items.name: Proper pushforward for relative characteristic classes
items.statement: For proper s:X→X' over S and F ULA/S, Rs*F is ULA/S and the duality-counit pushforward sends C_X/S(F) to C_X'/S(Rs*F).

items.name: Fibration formula in the fully ULA case
items.statement: Under B,C1 with F both Y-ULA and S-ULA, for any endomorphism α of F one has C_X/S(α)=δ!C_X/Y(α), where δ!:H0(K_X/Y)→H0(K_X/S) uses T12 and diagonal exchange.

items.name: Smooth fibration factor is top Chern
items.statement: Under C13 with g smooth of pure relative dimension r, δ! is cap product with c_r(f*Ω^∨_Y/S). In particular for smooth connected X/k and lisse finite-free L of rank n, C_X/k(L)=n c_dimX(Ω^∨_X/k).

items.name: Tensor-Hom transversality evaluation compatibility
items.statement: Under B,C1 and the two-map diagram(3.14.1), F on X and G on X', the paths of (3.14.2) from i*(F⊠S D_X'/S G)⊗p*δ!Λ to i!RHom(p2*G,p1!F) agree, with no ULA assumption. The evaluation in its proof includes the tensor factor p2*G.

items.name: Blowup derived decomposition
items.statement: For smooth X,Y over a perfect field with closed i:Y→X of codimension r≥1 and π:Bl_Y X→X, Rπ*π*F≃F⊕⊕_(t=1)^(r−1)i*i*F(-t)[-2t] for F∈Dctf(X,Λ), in the valid finite coefficient domain.

items.name: Blowup formula for cohomological characteristic class
items.statement: Under C16, X,Y connected, π*C_Bl/k(π*F)=C_X/k(F)+(r−1)i*C_Y/k(i*F). Rank-one Tate twists and even shifts cause no extra sign.

items.name: Blowup formula for Chow characteristic class
items.statement: Under C16 with the characteristic-class coefficient reduction fixed, π*cc_Bl(π*F)=cc_X(F)+(r−1)i*cc_Y(i*F) in CH0(X). Import the refined-Gysin blowup calculation with its transversality domain reconciled, rather than infer this from an unproved proper-pushforward conjecture.

items.statement: For finite-type h:X→S Noetherian and geometric specialization s←t, form X_s→X×S S_(s)←X_t and Ψ_h,s←t=i*Rj*. Retain the strict localization, geometric points and permitted constructibility hypotheses.

api.name: YangZhao25.C19.compatibility

tests.name: YangZhao25.C19.test3

items.name: Local Fourier total-dimension identity

items.name: Finite-to-adic lifting for the Fourier proof
items.statement: For the generic trait representation over finite residue field κ, after a finite extension E/Qℓ with residue κ, lift its K0 class via the surjective decomposition homomorphism, apply Laumon's local Fourier rank formula, and descend alternating dimensions. This is a K0 lift, not an arbitrary exact lift of each modular representation.

items.name: ULA of the zero-extended exponential family off the isolated point
items.statement: Under A, f:X→A1 and F ULA off a single closed x, pr2:(X×P1)\({x}×∞)→P1 is ULA for pr1*F⊗Lψ,!(f t'). Combine Laumon's kernel ULA and external-product acyclicity; local constancy on the affine parameter chart is a separate part.

items.name: Finite-cover ULA extension of the exponential family
items.statement: Under A and A05 there is a finite surjective integral curve P'→P1 and Ftilde∈Dctf(X×P',Λ) extending the exponential family on the affine parameter chart, ULA over P'. Descend the complex and its specified open identification from the absolute integral closure, not just an isomorphism class.

items.name: Absolutely integrally closed valuation extension
items.statement: For S=Spec V with V absolutely integrally closed valuation ring, X separated finitely presented over S, finite torsion coefficient setting(B) of Hansen–Scholze, restriction D_ULA(X/S)→Dcons(Xη) is an equivalence with inverse Rj*. Its image is perfect-constructible and it commutes with the specified flat base changes, duality and products.

items.name: Isolated Fourier stalk reduction
items.statement: In A06 the ∞-fiber is supported on x, and its Euler stalk dimension is −dimtot RΦ_x(F,f). The proof uses strict-local cohomology, smooth base change, projection against a flat local system, Ψ-goodness and A03; arbitrary nonproper base change is not substituted for Ψ-goodness.

items.name: Point-support class normalization
items.statement: Under A, for i:x→X a closed point mapping to a smooth curve Y, the untilded non-acyclicity class of i*V is χ(V) in H0_x(X,K_X/k)=Λ. Here C2 holds because x→Y has relative dualizing twist [-2]; the class is not χ times [k(x):k] before forgetting/pushing support.

items.name: Cohomological Milnor formula
items.statement: Under A, Y a smooth curve, f:X→Y separated finite type, x closed and F∈Dctf(X,Λ) with f ULA off x, C^{x}_X/Y/k(F)=−dimtot RΦ_xbar(F,f) in H0_x(X,K_X/k)=Λ. X need not be smooth or proper.
acceptance: For f=id_A1 and F=i*Λ at 0, Φ=Λ[1], so −dimtotΦ=1 and C^{0}=1.
For smooth f and lisse F, local acyclicity gives both sides zero.
proofSteps: First carry out the exponential-family argument A06/A08/A09 with a supplied nontrivial character, retaining G05/G06/G07 for its unsupplied geometric/Fourier leaves.
For an arbitrary coefficient ring in convention A, use Q01 and Q10. This proof order does not invoke the general-coefficient A10 to justify its own descent.

items.name: Finite-singularity fibration formula
items.statement: Under A, Y smooth connected curve, f:X→Y separated finite type, finite set Z of closed points and F ULA off Z, C_X/k(F)=c1(f*Ω^∨_Y/k) cap C_X/Y(F)−Σ_(x∈Z)dimtot RΦ_xbar(F,f)[x] in H0(X,K_X/k).
acceptance: For F=Λ on P1 and f=id, Z empty, the formula gives C_P1(Λ)=c1(TP1)=2[point].

items.name: Cohomological Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich
items.statement: Under A, X smooth connected curve and F∈Dctf(X,Λ) lisse off a finite Z, C_X/k(F)=rankF·c1(Ω^∨_X/k)−Σ_x a_x(F)[x], with a_x=rankFη−rankFx+Sw_xFη.
acceptance: For an origin skyscraper on a smooth curve, generic rank=0, stalk rank=1, Swan=0; a_0=−1 and the class is +[0].

items.name: Cohomological conductor formula
items.statement: Under A, f:X→Y proper, Y smooth connected curve, y closed and F∈Dctf(X,Λ) ULA off f^−1(y), ν_Y^−1(f*Ctilde^{f^−1(y)}_X/Y/k(F))=−a_y(Rf*F) in H0_y(Y,K_Y/k)=Λ. No source C2, smooth X, flatness or projectivity is required.
acceptance: For f=id_Y and F=i*Λ at y, the right side is −a_y=1 and agrees with the point support class.
For a positive-dimensional bad fiber no source C2 is silently imposed.

items.name: Global pushed localized-Chern conductor comparison
items.statement: Under A let f:X→Y proper flat between smooth schemes, dimX=n,dimY=1, smooth off fiber y. After pushing and forgetting support into H0(Y,K_Y/k), the tilded non-acyclicity expression equals the pushed cycle class of (-1)^n c^X_{n,Xy}(Ω1_X/Y)∩[X]. This is the proved weaker equality, not the supported equality of Remark6.8.
items.proofOutline: The source calculation (6.8.3), using proper trace compatibility, the curve fibration formula and the top tangent Chern normalization, identifies the pushed-and-forgotten non-acyclicity expression with the right side of J09. J09 identifies that expression with the pushed localized Chern class. Preserve the target H0(Y,K_Y/k); no source C2 or injective support-forgetting map is assumed. The source’s alternate cotangent-cycle calculation is J05–J06 plus J03.
acceptance: Use the A1 quadratic example in J09 to check that no supported equality is deduced from this global identity.
The proof uses neither the late Saito characteristic-class comparison M16 nor projectivity of f.

items.name: Finite étale descent for Saito's equality
items.statement: Under A, finite Galois k'/k of degree d invertible in Λ, if cl(cc)=C holds for (X_k',F_k') with X smooth, it holds for (X,F). Use σ*σ*F≃F⊗σ*Λ, M13 and C06, plus the finite étale cycle/class pushforward comparisons; do not claim σ*Λ constant. Divide only after applying cl into Λ-cohomology, not in integral Chow groups.
acceptance: For k=F2,k'=F4,Λ=F3, σ*Λ has Frobenius trace0 while Λ² has trace2; the proof still uses the common rank2 and divides2 only in Λ.
proofSteps: Projection formula gives σ*σ*F=F⊗σ*Λ. The rank-d lisse local system σ*Λ is not generally constant.
M13 and C06 multiply the two respective characteristic classes by d; M18 and C12 commute both with proper pushforward, with the étale base-field identification.

If equality holds upstairs, deduce d(cl(cc_X(F))−C_X/k(F))=0 in Λ-cohomology. Here d is a unit by hypothesis, so cancel it. This geometric-field descent is distinct from Q10 coefficient descent, which requires no invertible degree.

items.name: Finite local coefficient extension admitting an additive character
items.statement: Under A there exists a finite local finite étale Λ-algebra B, finite free of positive rank, and an injective additive character ψ:(Fp,+)→B×. Explicitly put R=Λ[T]/(Φp), choose a maximal ideal q of R, set B=R_q and ψ(a)=ζ^a for ζ the image of T. The finite coefficient ring is enlarged; the characteristic-p geometric field is unchanged.
items.locator: §6.3 and §6.4 p.45, missing coefficient-choice step; Stacks 00UB/00UC; pinned L05–L07
proofSteps: The polynomial Φp=1+T+⋯+T^(p−1) is monic of positive degree; L05 makes R finite free and nonzero. Since Λ is finite, R is a finite Artinian ring.
In R, ζ^p=1 and (ζ−1)Φp'(ζ)=pζ^(p−1). The right side is a unit since p is invertible in Λ, so Φp'(ζ) and ζ−1 are units. The standard étale criterion applies.

Choose q maximal. Localization is flat; L06 makes R→B surjective, hence B finite as a Λ-module. Its residue field is nonzero. Composition gives Λ-flatness; L07 gives a finite free Λ-module of positive rank. The localization remains étale: it is formally étale and finite presentation follows from finiteness over the Noetherian Λ.
Reduction modulo mΛ is a localization of the squarefree polynomial algebra κ[T]/Φp, hence a finite separable field κB. Thus mB=mΛB. The root ζ has order exactly p because ζ^p=1 and ζ−1 is a unit.
acceptance: For Λ=F2 and p=3, B=F4 works although [B:Λ]=2 is zero in Λ.
For Λ=Z/4 and p=3 the quadratic ring has 16 elements and retains characteristic 4.

items.name: Split detection after finite free coefficient extension
items.statement: Let Λ→B be a local map of nonzero local rings, B finite free over Λ, with B/mΛB nonzero. There is a Λ-linear λ:B→Λ with λ(1)=1. Consequently M→M⊗ΛB is split injective for every Λ-module M, and a complex or map is detected by tensoring with B. For finite free B, supported derived cohomology obeys H^i_Z(X,K⊗ΛB)≅H^i_Z(X,K)⊗ΛB, so the corresponding coefficient map is injective.
proofSteps: Apply L08 to Λ→B: modulo mΛ it is the injective unit map from a field to the nonzero algebra B/mΛB.
Tensor its retraction λ with any M. Flatness computes cohomology degreewise; positive finite free rank detects vanishing.

Choose a finite module basis of B only to verify the canonical comparison: tensoring is a finite direct sum, which derived sections with support preserve. The resulting comparison is independent of this verification basis.
acceptance: For F2→F4, a linear functional extracting the coefficient of 1 retracts the inclusion, while field trace(1)=0.
No division by rank B is used; residue reduction Λ→κ is not substituted for a faithful extension.

items.name: Finite free coefficient comparison for derived operations
items.statement: For a finite free commutative coefficient algebra Λ→B, scalar extension E(K)=K⊗ΛB is exact and symmetric monoidal between the actual derived sheaf categories. It preserves the finite-Tor constructible domain. The canonical comparisons with pullback, derived direct image, proper-support direct image and its exceptional right adjoint are isomorphisms wherever those operations have been constructed; units, counits, evaluation, composition and base-change transformations correspond. In particular E(K_X/S,Λ)≅K_X/S,B and E(RHomΛ(F,K))≅RHomB(EF,EK).
items.locator: §§2.1,3.1 and4.5 applied after coefficient extension; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/E3; geometric instantiation is conditional on existing B02
proofSteps: Restriction of B-sheaves to Λ-sheaves is exact and conservative. Its left adjoint is exact because B is flat. For this finite-free extension its right adjoint HomΛ(B,−) is exact as well.

This node is the formal coefficient-comparison interface only: it does not construct the geometric operations of B02. The geometric consumers separately import those operations. After restriction, the coefficient comparisons for additive derived functors identify with finite direct-sum comparisons; for exceptional pullback use its adjunction to Rf! and dualizability of the finite-free constant coefficient object. This does not assert any new constructibility theorem on arbitrary bases.

Derived adjunction gives RHomB(F⊗B,K⊗B)=RHomΛ(F,K⊗B), and finite direct sums commute with RHom in its second variable. Compare the canonical tensor map through a basis to get the asserted isomorphism, even when F is not locally a perfect complex on X.

The identifications are the canonical mates, so carry units/counits, tensor evaluation and the diagrams defining exchange. Enhance using the existing E1/E3 construction, not arbitrary choices of triangulated cones.
acceptance: For B=Λ the maps are identities.
For a finite local coefficient ring with nilpotents the assertion uses free B, not the nonflat residue quotient.

items.name: ULA preserved and detected by coefficient enlargement
items.statement: Under B with a finite local coefficient ring and finite faithfully free local coefficient extension Λ→B, a constructible finite-Tor F is ULA for f iff F⊗ΛB is. The equivalence holds after every geometric base change.
proofSteps: Use the strict-local specialization comparison defining ULA. Q03 identifies the comparison for F⊗B with the original comparison tensored by B.
Q02 detects that its cone is zero. Repeat after every base change; no alteration or extra geometric smoothness is required.
acceptance: An origin skyscraper for id_A1 remains non-ULA after F2→F4.
The zero complex is ULA before and after extension.

items.name: Relative trace commutes with finite free coefficient extension
items.statement: For F∈Dctf(X/S,Λ) and the coefficient extension of Q04, the coefficient map sends the relative fixed-locus trace of a cohomological correspondence to its B-linear trace. In particular C_X/S,Λ(F) maps to C_X/S,B(F⊗B), without a factor rankΛB.
proofSteps: Apply the strong symmetric monoidal coefficient functor and the Q03 duality comparison to coevaluation, the correspondence morphism and evaluation. Their composite is the B-valued trace.
Use Q04 to retain the ULA domain. This is extension of coefficients, whereas C06 describes tensoring by a lisse Λ-module and then taking a Λ-valued trace; they are different operations.
acceptance: At a point trB(idB)=1B after extending Λ in degree zero, even if rankΛB=0 in Λ.
A shift by one carries −1Λ to −1B.

items.name: Coefficient comparison for the diagonal defect
items.statement: For the finite free coefficient extension and diagram D, the canonical coefficient comparisons identify the transversality map c, the closed-diagonal defect δ∆F, and the coefficient triangle K_X/Y→K_X/S→K_X/Y/S with their B versions. C1 is preserved and C2 is preserved and reflected.
proofSteps: The exchange morphism is a composite of the unit/counit and projection comparison, all matched by Q03.
The actual closed-diagonal formula i!(F⊗f*Rj*Λ) therefore commutes with E; its coherent cofiber triangle is carried to the B triangle by exactness.

The invertible evaluation in C1 and its locally constant coefficients persist. Q02 identifies support cohomology with its finite-free scalar extension, proving both directions of the C2 vanishing test.
acceptance: The map for a smooth relative curve still carries twist(1)[2]; coefficient change removes neither.
For X=Y=S a point and Z=X, H0(K_Z/Y)=Λ is nonzero and stays nonzero.

items.name: Supported non-acyclicity classes commute with coefficients
items.statement: Under D,C1,C3 and the coefficient extension of Q04, Ctilde^Z_Λ(F) maps to Ctilde^Z_B(F⊗B). If C2 holds, the same equality holds for C^Z with ordinary relative-dualizing coefficients. This is equality of the specifically constructed supported classes, not merely their images after forgetting support.
proofSteps: Transport the diagonal characteristic correspondence using Q05 and apply the defect comparison Q06.

The intermediate defect complex is supported on Z, and its localization factorization is carried along the natural coefficient functor. Thus the construction through τ* and τ! in (4.5.3), including its support, agrees.
If C2 holds, Q06 compares the isomorphism ν of (4.2.7); uniqueness of its inverse image gives the untilded identity.
acceptance: A rank-one point skyscraper retains class 1B, not rankΛB.
With Z empty both supported classes are zero.

items.name: Finite free coefficients commute with nearby and vanishing cycles
items.statement: For the specialization functor Ψ=i*Rj* of C19 and finite free Λ→B, EΨ(F)≅Ψ(EF), with the specialization map and inertia action. Hence E RΦ(F,f)≅RΦ(EF,f). Constructibility and finite-Tor assertions retain the source hypotheses from G06.
proofSteps: Apply the direct-image and pullback comparisons of Q03 to the actual geometric-specialization diagram.
Carry the specialization unit and its coherent cofiber through the exact functor. Inertia acts through natural automorphisms of this diagram, so the comparison is equivariant.
acceptance: For a point skyscraper ΦΛ=Λ[1] extends to B[1].
This comparison does not assert arbitrary geometric base-change goodness of Ψ.

items.name: Swan and total dimension invariant under coefficient enlargement
items.statement: Under A, for B as in Q01 and a bounded finite-Tor inertia complex V with finite wild ramification, dimtotB(V⊗ΛB)=dimtotΛ(V) as integers. Alternating ordinary dimension is likewise unchanged when each side is measured over its own residue field.
proofSteps: Since B/mΛB=κB, derived residue reduction identifies (V⊗ΛB)⊗B^LκB with (V⊗Λ^Lκ)⊗κκB. Field extension is flat, so cohomology and its dimensions are unchanged.

On each finite-image positive ramification group, invariant vectors are kernels of the finite matrix of operators (g−1). Flat field extension preserves these kernels and their dimensions, hence every codimension entering the Swan sum. The ramification filtration and its weights are unchanged.
Take the bounded alternating sum for V. This proves coefficient invariance given the conductor construction; it does not construct the ramification filtration or the local Fourier theorem.
acceptance: A trivial rank-r complex in degree zero keeps total dimension r, not [κB:κ]r.
Shifting by one negates both integer invariants.

items.name: Descent of the local Milnor identity from character coefficients
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of A10, assume the character-admitting case of its geometric proof has been established for F⊗ΛB with B from Q01. Then the identity C^x_Λ(F)=−dimtotΛ RΦ_x(F,f) holds in Λ. No condition that rankΛB be invertible is required.
items.locator: §6.4 completion of the coefficient-choice step, E8
proofSteps: Q04 preserves the ULA hypotheses and Q06 preserves the support comparison needed to form C^x.
Use Q07 on the left side, Q08 on the vanishing-cycle complex and Q09 on its integer total dimension. The hypothesized B identity is exactly the image of the desired Λ identity.
Apply injectivity Λ→B from Q02. Neither normalized field trace nor reduction Λ→κ is used to detect equality.

The argument retains the full Z/4-valued equality when B=Z/4[T]/(T²+T+1).

items.name: Finite étale pushforward of characteristic cycles
items.statement: Under A for a finite étale map u:X'→X between smooth schemes over k and F'∈Dctf(X',Λ), CC(Ru*F')=u_*CC(F') as integral cycles on T*X, where T*X'≅X'×X T*X and u_* is proper cycle pushforward.
items.locator: Saito, On the proper push-forward…, arXiv1607.03156v1 pp.2–4, Lemma2; finite étale case used in YZ(6.13.2)
proofSteps: The source Lemma2 proves the stronger finite-on-support case by the Milnor formula: vanishing cycles on a finite fiber split as a finite direct sum and local intersection numbers satisfy projection. We import only its finite étale special case.

For this special case, trivialize u in an étale cover of X. The pushforward becomes a finite direct sum, so CC equality follows from M06 additivity and étale pullback. Equality of cycles descends from this cover; rational equivalence descent is not asserted.
For finite local coefficients reduce to the residue field exactly as in Saito18 p.1; finite direct image and flat pullback match that derived reduction in this finite étale setting.
acceptance: For the trivial disjoint degree-d cover, the cycle is the sum of the d component cycles.
A connected finite étale cover need not have constant pushforward local system.

items.name: Finite étale pushforward of degree-zero characteristic classes
items.statement: With u and F' as in M17, u_*cc_X'(F')=cc_X(Ru*F') in CH0(X), and the cycle map cl carries this equality to the corresponding proper pushforward equality in H0(X,K_X/k). For u:X_k'→X, the canonical étale identification K_X_k'/k≅K_X_k'/k' compares the relative field conventions.
items.locator: Saito18 Lemma2 followed by zero-section refined Gysin; YZ(6.13.2)
proofSteps: The square of zero sections for T*X'≅X'×X T*X is cartesian. Proper-pushforward compatibility of refined Gysin from M05 gives 0_X!u_*CC=u_*0_X'!CC.
Use the smooth-scheme definition cc=0!CC in M04, then the proper compatibility of cl already assigned to M05.

For the finite separable constant-field extension, the structural map Spec k'→Spec k is étale of relative dimension zero; its exceptional pullback is ordinary pullback with no twist/shift. Transitivity compares the two dualizing conventions.
acceptance: On a closed point of degree d the Chow pushforward has multiplicity d before applying cl.
No inverse of d is introduced in the integral Chow group.

items.statement: Let X be finite type over a field, Z⊂X closed, and K a bounded complex of finite-rank locally free O_X-modules. items.statement: Let D⊂X be an effective Cartier divisor on a finite-type scheme over a field. For K=[O_X→O_X(D)] in degrees −1,0 with the canonical section, H0(K)=i_*O_D(D). The total localized class acting on [X] equals [X]+[D] (ordinary degree zero plus supported degree one), so localized c1(K)∩[X]=[D] and all higher localized components on [X] vanish.

There the support pushforward is injective and 0→E_X→E_X(D)→i_*E(D)→0 computes the ordinary total Chern quotient. The required deformation and bivariant compatibility are the J01/J02 supplier obligations, not a new conductor theorem.

items.name: Section intersection equals the localized top Chern class
items.statement: Let X be a pure d-dimensional finite-type scheme over a field, E a rank-n vector bundle, n≥1, s a section, and Z its scheme-theoretic zero locus. With E placed in degree zero in K=[O_X→E], the refined intersection of the zero and s sections equals c_n^X_Z(K)∩[X] in CH_{d−n}(Z), using the localized class J02. No regularity of Z, transverse-zero assumption or properness of X is imposed.
items.locator: Saito1704.04832v4 Lemma2.1.4 and full proof, p.31; Kato–Saito2004 Proposition2.3.1(6), Lemma2.3.2
items.proofOutline: Use linearity on the fundamental cycle and proper bivariant compatibility to reduce to integral X. If s=0, J02 global normalization with Z=X and zero-section self-intersection give c_n(E)∩[X] directly. Otherwise blow up the ideal generated by the components of s. On the blowup this ideal is invertible; factoring out its local generator gives a primitive vector, hence a line subbundle L=O(D)⊂π*E with locally free quotient F of rank n−1. The pulled-back section of L cuts out the effective Cartier divisor D, including its multiplicities. J10 and the localized Whitney formula give c_{n−1}(F|D)∩[D]. The excess-intersection formula gives exactly the same class for the refined intersection. Push it back to Z. No resolution of singularities is used.
externalInputs: J02 must also supply the localized Whitney formula for the triangle [O→L]→[O→E]→F with the stated rank thresholds (Kato–Saito Proposition2.3.1(4), whose proof is referred to Abbes).
acceptance: For E=O_A1, s=x^m, the class is m[0].
For E=O_A2² and s=(x²,0), the excess line bundle is trivial, so the top supported class is zero on the divisor V(x²), despite its nonempty zero scheme.
For s=0 in O_P1(1), the degree is one; the proof must handle this case before blowing up the zero ideal.

items.proofOutline: Flatness over the integral curve makes every nonempty component dominate Y. Generic smoothness makes the line-to-bundle map nonzero at every generic point, hence injective on the smooth reduced X. The usual exact sequence of differentials identifies its cokernel. Since k is perfect, a local uniformizer at a closed point generates the curve differentials after shrinking. Off the bad fiber f is smooth, so df is a subbundle inclusion and has no zero. All these constructions precede any characteristic-cycle theorem.

items.name: Cotangent correspondence pushforward on supported cycles
items.statement: Let f:X→Y be a morphism of smooth pure-dimensional k-schemes, dimensions n,m; let B⊂X be closed with f|B proper, and C⊂T*X closed over B. Define f∘C as the image in T*Y of the inverse image of C in X×Y T*Y. Compose the lci Gysin map along X×Y T*Y→T*X with proper pushforward to obtain f!:CH_n(C)→CH_m(f∘C). When dim C≤n and dim(f∘C)≤m, this is a map on integral top-dimensional cycles Z_n(C)→Z_m(f∘C).

items.name: Zero-section and fiber coefficients for a curve target
items.statement: Let k be perfect, f:X→Y a morphism of smooth irreducible schemes with dim X=n and dim Y=1, and C=⋃C_a⊂T*X conical with each C_a of dimension n. Assume f proper on B=C∩zero_X and choose dense open V⊂Y on which f is properly C-transversal. For A=Σm_a[C_a], v a closed point of V, and A_v the signed properly transversal pullback, one has f!A=−deg(A_v,zero_Xv)[zero_Y]+Σ_{y∉V}deg(A,df)_{Xy}[T*_yY] as integral cycles. For the fiber at v, work on a smooth neighborhood of B∩X_v, where transversality ensures f is smooth; singularities outside this support do not enter the fiber cotangent intersection. The boundary intersection uses a local uniformizer, is a class in CH0(B∩X_y), and its degree is relative to k(y), not k.
items.locator: Saito1704.04832v4 Lemma2.1.2, (2.5), Lemma2.1.3(2), pp.29–30; complete displayed proofs read
items.proofOutline: Proper transversality places the support over V in zero_Y. For its coefficient, commute the two cartesian cotangent/fiber squares with refined Gysin and proper pushforward. The signed convention for i_v! contributes (−1)^codim(Xv,X)=−1. For each missing y intersect with the local section dt of T*Y. Its pullback is df, and the projection formula gives the coefficient of the cotangent fiber. Conicality gives independence from rescaling dt by a unit. This cycle calculation uses no conductor theorem, no global Saito comparison and no projectivity hypothesis.
acceptance: For f=id_Y and A=[zero_Y], the signed fiber pullback has degree −1, so the coefficient of zero_Y is +1.
For t=x^m on A1 with char(k)∤m, f![zero_X]=m[zero_Y]+(m−1)[T*_0Y].
Replacing A by −A negates both coefficients.
externalInputs: The signed properly transversal cotangent pullback and its expected-dimension compatibility are the existing M01/M05 supplier interfaces; the full Saito2017 Definition7.1 proof chain is not newly read here.

items.name: Top Chern identity for a line pulled back from a curve
items.statement: Let X be smooth pure dimension n≥1, Y a smooth curve, f:X→Y, and K=[f*Ω1_Y/k→Ω1_X/k] in degrees −1,0. In integral CH^n(X), (−1)^n c_n(K)=c_n(T_X/k)−f*c1(T_Y/k)·c_{n−1}(T_X/k). The identity depends on the virtual bundles only; it does not assume injectivity of the displayed differential.
items.locator: Whitney and dual Chern identities from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5; written calculation expanding Yang–Zhao(6.8.3)
items.proofOutline: Write α=f*c1(ΩY). Since CH²(Y)=0, α²=0. Thus c(K)=c(ΩX)/(1+α)=c(ΩX)(1−α). Extract degree n and use c_i(ΩX)=(−1)^i c_i(TX), c1(ΩY)=−c1(TY). All signs and coefficients are integral; no factorial denominators or rational Riemann–Roch appear.
acceptance: For n=1 the formula is −c1(ΩX)+f*c1(ΩY)=c1(TX)−f*c1(TY).
For a product F×Y→Y, with F smooth of dimension n−1, the right side is zero by Whitney.
The inverse (1+α)^{-1}=1−α requires α²=0; it is not a formula for an arbitrary line class on a higher-dimensional base.

items.name: Smooth proper Euler class from the existing trace
items.statement: Under coefficient convention A, for a smooth proper k-scheme Z of pure dimension d, Tr_Z cl(c_d(T_Z)∩[Z]) equals the image in Λ of the alternating dimension of RΓ(Z_bar,Λ) after derived residue reduction. The same formula applies to each geometric fiber of a smooth proper morphism. This is a Λ-valued statement; by itself it does not prove equality of two integral Euler numbers.
items.locator: Yang–Zhao Proposition3.11 and (3.13.3), specialized to Z→Spec(k); coefficient convention A
items.proofOutline: C14 identifies the characteristic class of the constant sheaf with its top tangent Chern class. C12 pushes it to the characteristic class of RΓ. At a point this is the categorical trace of the identity of the perfect coefficient complex, namely its Euler rank; derived residue reduction computes that rank in Λ. No characteristic-cycle index theorem or projectivity assumption is used.
acceptance: For P1 the top tangent Chern degree and Euler rank are both 2, interpreted in Λ.
For a smooth proper genus-one curve both sides vanish.
With Λ=F3, the equality of residues 1=4 in Λ does not certify equality 1=4 in Z.

items.name: Global image of the localized cotangent Chern term
items.statement: Under A, let f:X→Y be proper flat with X smooth pure dimension n≥1, Y a smooth connected curve, and f smooth over V=Y−{y}. Put r=Euler rank of Rf*Λ on V and β=c^X_{n,Xy}(Ω1_X/Y)∩[X]∈CH0(X_y), with i:X_y→X. In H0(Y,K_Y/k), cl(f_*i_*((−1)^nβ))=cl(f_*(c_n(TX)∩[X]))−r·cl(c1(TY)∩[Y]). Support has been forgotten on the left. The equality is not asserted in H0_y(Y,K_Y/k).
items.locator: Written bridge for Yang–Zhao2209.11086v4 Remark6.8(6.8.2–3); Kato–Saito Proposition2.3.1(1); J07–J08
items.proofOutline: J02 sends i_*β to c_n(K)∩[X]. J07 and the Chow projection formula reduce the identity to determining the cohomological image of f_*(c_{n−1}(TX)∩[X])∈CH1(Y). Since Y is integral, this is m[Y] for an integer m. Choose a geometric point of V and use flat/refined base change to compute m from that smooth proper fiber. The tangent exact sequence has trivial rank-one quotient on the fiber, so its degree-(n−1) Chern class is the top tangent class of the fiber. J08 identifies the image of m in Λ with r. Apply the cycle map and its proper/pullback compatibilities. No cancellation in CH or injection of the support-forgetting map is used.
acceptance: For a smooth product F×Y→Y, β=0 and the two global terms cancel.

For k algebraically closed of characteristic 5, Λ=F3 and f:A1→A1, t=x², the signed local term is −[0] and has nonzero class −1 in H0_{0}(A1,K)=F3, while its image in H0(A1,K)=H²(A1,F3(1)) is zero. Thus global vanishing does not imply supported vanishing.
The fiber computation determines m modulo the coefficient characteristic for this argument; an integer Gauss–Bonnet theorem is not inferred from a single finite coefficient ring.

items.name: Saito's conjecture on characteristic classes (statement only)
items.statement: For a closed subscheme X of a smooth scheme over a perfect field k and F ∈ D_ctf(X, Λ), C_{X/k}(F) = cl(cc_X(F)) in H⁰(X, K_{X/k}). Not proved in general; Theorem 6.13 (M16) is the smooth quasi-projective case.

routes.title: Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves, Part II: relative categorical traces
routes.reason: Reuse the same pending continuation proposed in PAPER-ABE-25, not a parallel non-acyclicity roadmap. Yang–Zhao adds the general-base transversality defect, supported characteristic classes and coherent infinity-categorical fibration proof beyond EDC.8 and beyond Abe's two-categorical trace prefix.
routes.brief: Extend the pending RelativeTraces brief from PAPER-ABE-25 without duplicating it. Import Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0, EDC.1:adjoint, EDC.2:trace-purity, EDC.3, EDC.4, EDC.8), Enhanced derived categories of sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0,E1,E3,E5:abstract), and the generic existing triangulated K0. First close the Noetherian-base/coefficient six-operation and ULA-dualizability interfaces; ordinary field duality does not suffice. Construct generalized transversality c, its diagonal evaluation condition C1, the explicit closed-diagonal defect functor and K_X/Y/S. Build relative characteristic classes with ULA globally or uniquely extended across H0/H1 support vanishing. Define Ctilde with coefficients K_X/Y/S under C1,C3, and only then C^Z with coefficients K_X/S under C2. Prove base change, proper pushforward, independent étale locality in X and Y, and trait specialization with the exact source/target vanishings. Upgrade the six-functor correspondence construction to the coherent infinity setting, importing all generic stable-category, lifting and nine-diagram machinery from EDS. Prove the fibration equality C_X/S=δ!C_X/Y+C^Z under C1–C3 by either fully recorded proof. Under perfect char-p k, finite local ℓ≠p coefficients, separated f:X→smooth curve and ULA off a closed x, prove C^{x}=−dimtot RΦ_x without smoothness of X; deduce the finite-Z and cohomological GOS formulas. For proper f and ULA off f^−1(y), prove ν_Y^−1 f*Ctilde=−a_y(Rf*F) without imposing source C2. Import the earlier local-Fourier/ULA-extension prefix from LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCyclesPartIIGeneralBasesFourier. Do not import the late Artin theorem or Saito comparison back into that prefix. The non-isolated localized-Bloch equality stays conjectural; only its stated global pushforward comparison is a theorem here. Prove finite faithfully free coefficient transport of ULA, transversality, supported non-acyclicity classes and local Milnor descent (Q04–Q07,Q10). Import the generic coefficient functor and split-detection facts from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/E3. Preserve the supported factorization itself. Do not multiply a B-valued trace by rankΛB, or divide by that rank; a Λ-linear retraction detects equality even for F2→F4. For A14, use J08’s smooth-proper trace calculation and J09’s integral Whitney/projection calculation after applying the cycle map. Retain only the global pushed equality; do not require the late microlocal Saito comparison or a projective global index theorem.

routes.title: Lefschetz pencils, nearby cycles and vanishing cycles, Part II: general bases and local Fourier transforms

routes.brief: Extend, rather than duplicate, the GeneralBasesFourier continuation proposed in PAPER-ABE-25. Import Lefschetz pencils, nearby cycles and vanishing cycles (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0) for ordinary strict-local RΨ/RΦ, Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0) for coefficients, and Enhanced derived categories of sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0–E3) for the actual enhancement. Retain the existing early Swan-module and modular K0/decomposition interfaces; no late geometric Artin theorem is needed. Construct general-base geometric-specialization nearby cycles and prove the applicable goodness, constructibility and base-change results from their primary sources. In the perfect char-p finite-local coefficient setting, construct the chosen nontrivial additive-character kernel, and prove coefficient enlargement/descent when the original ring lacks that character. Prove the precise alternating identity −dimtot RΦ_0(F,id)=χΨ_pr2(pr1*F⊗Lψ,!(t/t')) at (0,0'). Construct the absolute-integral-closure Rj* extension with finite Tor and ULA, then descend both complex and open identification to a finite integral cover of the parameter curve. Prove support at the isolated point and the strict-local Fourier stalk comparison using Ψ-goodness. Export those identities to RelativeTraces' cohomological Milnor proof. Tests must distinguish a full-trait constant sheaf from j! of its generic restriction, preserve the degree-one negative sign, and reject the nonexistent character F3→F2×. The pure Fourier theorem precedes both the late Artin theorem and all characteristic-cycle comparisons. Before choosing ψ, construct a finite local coefficient enlargement via a maximal localization of Λ[T]/Φp, importing the pinned monic power basis, Artinian-localization surjectivity and finite-flat local freeness. Establish nearby-cycle coefficient comparison and invariance of the integer Swan/total dimension through residue-field extension. The extension degree need not be prime to ℓ. General local Fourier and modular-to-adic lifting proofs remain required; coefficient descent alone does not prove them.

routes.title: Étale Duality and Perverse Sheaves, Part II: characteristic cycles and polar bounds
routes.reason: Reuse the pending microlocal continuation from PAPER-SHENDE-TSIMERMAN-17. Its brief already demands a separately sourced positive-characteristic Beilinson–Saito branch. This extraction supplies that branch's precise characteristic-class comparison target; it does not infer it from characteristic-zero conormal topology.
routes.brief: Extend the existing pending Microlocal brief, preserving its characteristic-zero polar-bound branch and its single ownership. Import Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0,EDC.3,EDC.4,EDC.8), Lefschetz pencils, nearby cycles and vanishing cycles (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0 and pencil geometry), and the earlier outputs of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartIIRelativeTraces. Over a perfect field of characteristic p>0 with finite local coefficients of residue characteristic ℓ≠p, construct cotangent C-transversality, micro-support, Beilinson's singular support and the integral Saito characteristic cycle characterized by the isolated Milnor formula. Prove CC(Λ_X)=(-1)^dimX[zero section], shift/additivity, étale locality and finite-free lisse rank twisting. Construct the degree-zero class cc_X=0_X!CC(F); distinguish it from the total characteristic class for embeddable singular schemes. Import integral Chow/refined-Gysin/Chern operations and the rank-threshold localized-perfect-complex construction from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 (J01–J03/J10); EDC.3 supplies their étale cycle realization. Own only the cotangent presentation and microlocal applications J04–J06/M08. Prove good-pencil existence and the two matched Chow/cohomological induction identities, retaining smooth properly transversal fibers for divω and the actual quasi-projective reduction, prime-to-ℓ field extension and smooth codimension-two center hypotheses. Repair finite étale descent with F⊗σ*Λ and rank twisting, not the false constant-direct-sum identification. Final theorem: for smooth quasi-projective X/k and F∈Dctf(X,Λ), cl(cc_X(F))=C_X/k(F) in H0(X,K_X/k). This is not the full embeddable-singular conjecture. Define the non-isolated candidate (f*dt)!CC(F), prove its finite-support comparison only, and retain Conjecture6.10 and the supported Bloch formula as explicit non-theorems. Obtain the final UYZ journal pencil/blowup statements before closing this route. Use Saito18 Lemma2 in the finite étale domain for the cycle pushforward step, then commute the zero-section refined Gysin with proper pushforward to obtain the Chow class identity (M17–M18). Retain the independent quasi-projective good-pencil gap.
